candidates.title: Prepare resume facts for repeated application forms

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare resume information repeatedly for forms tailored to one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet that maps supplied resume facts to operator-entered application field labels, with uncertain or missing values flagged.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a new practice application and provides fictional resume text plus its field labels.
steps: Enter fictional resume facts and the target field labels.
Use a documented schema to extract candidate values from the supplied text.
Mark unsupported or absent facts as blank.
Compare each suggestion with a prepared answer key.
Have a person approve or correct values before any manual form entry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed fictional resume and field list, every populated suggestion must match the answer key and every absent fact must remain blank.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies the form labels, checks all suggested values, protects any real resume data, and manually enters and submits the application.
unverified: Whether company-specific forms expose stable labels
Whether extraction remains accurate on varied layouts
No browser form reading or submission capability is documented

ease.reason: A beginner can try structured extraction from supplied resume text; n8n documents schema-based extraction but not form reading.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers or career-support services may value less repeated entry; the post establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic review sheet is bounded for four weeks; company-specific form layouts and live entry are outside the documented reference.

autonomy.reason: Structured extraction is documented, but no form automation is; a person must verify and enter every response.

evidence.reason: The post reports a daily two-hour chore for forms tailored to one or two companies; wider recurrence and buyer evidence are absent.

candidates.reason: Concrete repeated chore and a matching structured-text extraction reference support a scoped review-sheet experiment; conservative mean is below six.

candidates.title: Draft compact summaries of long email threads

demandEvidence.chore: Create a compact summary and prefill a draft from a long email conversation while retaining a reference to the original email.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I use it to create draft prefill with the good knowledge + compact history of the conversation with each mail resume

experimentPlan.output: A draft summary of a supplied fictional email thread with an operator-provided reference label and a compact context block.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a fictional thread and its stable test label into the prototype.
steps: Keep the supplied reference label beside the input.
Draft a short summary of the thread and its stated question.
Flag names, dates, or commitments that need checking.
Compare the summary with a prepared checklist.
Have a person verify the summary before using it to prefill any draft.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: The summary must preserve the thread’s central request and critical decisions from a prepared fictional example, with no invented detail.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies test text, checks the reference and every summary, and handles any real mailbox access or sending; the current source packet has no implementation reference.
unverified: Immutable email ID behavior is unverified
Summary accuracy across varied threads is untested
Privacy and access controls for real email are unresolved

ease.reason: A fictional text-only mock is possible, but no supplied implementation reference documents email intake or summarization.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: client-facing professionals might value compact thread review; this request gives no buyer or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week offline mock can use fictional threads, while email access, stable IDs, and summary accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed draft loop is review-heavy and no software capability is documented; a person must supply and verify every thread.

evidence.reason: The retained post describes compacting long email history and referencing messages, but not repeated volume or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The retained spans describe a concrete email summarization and reference need, but no supplied implementation source supports its mechanics; mean remains below six.

candidates.title: Prepare full-size product images for messaging

demandEvidence.chore: Correct product images that appear as cropped squares in a messaging app, repeatedly selecting the full-size image instead.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I wish the image added for a product on the messaging app would default to the full size image and not a cut off square one, have to go in and correct it all the time.

experimentPlan.output: A human-reviewed image preparation mock that takes a supplied product image and produces a full-size copy plus a preview for a messaging listing.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides a synthetic product image that has appeared cropped in a messaging listing.
steps: Load the supplied image into a simple test page.
Create a full-size copy without changing the source file.
Show a preview of the expected messaging display.
Compare the preview with the operator’s expected result.
Let a person approve and upload any corrected image manually.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: The generated preview must preserve the full source image and match the expected uncropped result for a small synthetic test set.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies licensed test images, checks visual quality and uploads approved images; no messaging-app integration or image capability is documented in the supplied references.
unverified: Actual messaging-app image rules are unknown
No supplied implementation reference documents image conversion
Automated upload and default-setting capability are absent

ease.reason: A student can mock a preview using test images, but supplied sources do not document image-processing tools or app rules.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small merchants may value fewer repeated image corrections; this single request shows no willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic preview test is bounded, but correct platform-specific image handling is unknown.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable preview is proposed, but image preparation and upload are unsupported; a person must inspect and apply changes.

evidence.reason: The post says the image requires repeated correction, but provides no example formats, platform rules, or corroborated demand.

candidates.reason: A recurring correction is stated, but no supplied implementation evidence supports image transformation or messaging-app handling; mean is below six.

candidates.title: Check whether a Shopify app has security verification

demandEvidence.chore: Find out whether a Shopify app has an official security review or verification mark before installing it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can we know if a Shopify app is secure and trustworthy? Is there any official badge, certification, or verification mark that indicates an app has been reviewed and approved by Shopify for security?

experimentPlan.output: A source-linked checklist that records public security signals for one named test app and leaves unsupported checks marked unknown.
inputs: Public official policy pages supplied by an operator
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator asks for a review of a test app before installation.
steps: List the security questions the operator wants answered.
Gather the official public pages the operator supplies.
Record only explicit statements and link each to its page.
Mark missing or ambiguous evidence as unknown.
Have a person review the checklist and decide whether to install.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Every checklist statement must link to a supplied official source that explicitly supports it; unknowns must not be presented as a security verdict.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person chooses sources, checks all claims, and makes the installation decision; this is not a security audit or certification.
unverified: No official Shopify security badge or policy is identified in the retained post
No supplied implementation reference supports web research or security assessment
Completeness and freshness of official sources are unresolved

ease.reason: A person can assemble a small checklist, but no supplied implementation source supports automated source retrieval or assessment.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: store operators may value clearer app checks; the request establishes no paid service demand.

feasibility.reason: A source-linked manual checklist is testable in four weeks, but it cannot establish software security.

autonomy.reason: The loop depends on human source selection and judgment; no automated verification capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The post asks about official verification but does not provide policy details, a specific app, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The question identifies a security-verification need but the supplied spans and references do not establish an official testable checklist; mean is below six.

rejected.title: App review: Elfsight AI Chatbot pending
rejected.reason: The retained span asks for an estimated review timeline for one pending app approval. This is a one-off status inquiry, not a repeatable service chore; no broader duty is supplied.

rejected.title: Streaming service discovery
rejected.reason: The supplied excerpt only asks whether people bounce between streaming services to find something to watch. It does not identify a bounded task or evidence for the assigned professional-services buyer; more context is missing from the supplied excerpt.

rejected.title: WhatsApp Business connection troubleshooting
rejected.reason: The retained context describes one account’s Make authorization flow stuck before Meta authorization despite browser retries. This is a one-off integration bug report, not a repeatable chore suitable for an independent service.

rejected.title: Browser-based white noise fan
rejected.reason: The excerpt describes a consumer white-noise app and a personal preference, not a concrete professional-services chore; proposed buyer fit would be invented.

rejected.title: General startup operations management
rejected.reason: The supplied excerpt says only that a provider manages startup operations. It names no specific task to scope, so a duty or experiment cannot be inferred.

rejected.title: Shopify Payments payout follow-up
rejected.reason: The retained span describes one user repeatedly asking support about a frozen payout. Building a service around payment-risk escalation would be unsafe and cannot affect Shopify’s decision; the excerpt supplies no safe independent resolution task.

steps.message: Assessed all ten sealed discussion identities. Four concrete chores received five-criterion scoped assessments; each remains below the six-point threshold. The remaining six were excluded for one-off, vague, or buyer-mismatched evidence. No post proposed.
